subject.title: RFC: policy on agent-directed instruction content in docs

question: Should ClawHub adopt a public acceptability rule for agent-directed instructions in SKILL.md/README content, and where should that rule live?
rationale: The request defines a marketplace trust boundary rather than fixing broken current behavior, and current docs/source only cover adjacent execution, metadata, and scanner-review concepts.

options.title: Adopt Public Policy Guidance
options.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public publishing or acceptable-use docs and mirror the internal security invariant in specs.

options.title: Fold Into Related RFCs
options.body: Resolve this only as part of the declared-capability and cross-asset review RFCs so manifest declarations, scanner signals, and policy wording ship together.

options.title: Keep Boundary Internal For Now
options.body: Leave the decision to ClawScan/moderator judgment without publishing a submitter-facing rule yet, accepting less predictability for authors.

recommendation.title: Adopt Public Policy Guidance
recommendation.body: Add concise allowed, needs-review, and not-allowed examples to public publishing or acceptable-use docs and mirror the internal security invariant in specs.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest individual routing signal for the CODEOWNERS-listed security docs and ClawScan paths that would encode this boundary.
